Let \( a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots \) be the unique sequence of nonnegative integers less than 397 with \( a_0 = 1 \) and

\[ a_{n+1}(a_n + 1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397} \]

for all nonnegative integers \( n \). Given that \( a_{2026} = 9 \), compute the remainder when \( a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_{2026} \) is divided by 397.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Work modulo \(397\). Since \(397\) is prime and the sequence is defined for all \(n\), no term is \(0\) or \(-1\), so every \(a_n\) is invertible modulo \(397\).

Let

\[
b_n \equiv a_n^{-1} \pmod{397}.
\]

From

\[
a_{n+1}(a_n+1)^2 \equiv a_n,
\]

divide by \(a_{n+1}a_n\):

\[
\frac1{a_{n+1}} \equiv \frac{(a_n+1)^2}{a_n}
= a_n+2+\frac1{a_n}.
\]

Thus

\[
b_{n+1} \equiv b_n+2+a_n \pmod{397},
\]

so

\[
a_n \equiv b_{n+1}-b_n-2 \pmod{397}.
\]

Summing from \(n=0\) to \(2026\),

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv b_{2027}-b_0-2\cdot 2027 \pmod{397}.
\]

We have \(b_0=a_0^{-1}=1\). Given \(a_{2026}=9\),

\[
b_{2026}\equiv 9^{-1}\pmod{397}.
\]

Since \(9\cdot 44=396\equiv -1\), we get \(9^{-1}\equiv -44\equiv 353\). Then

\[
b_{2027}\equiv b_{2026}+2+a_{2026}
\equiv 353+2+9=364 \pmod{397}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv 364-1-4054
\equiv -3691 \equiv 279 \pmod{397}.
\]

\[
\boxed{279}
\]
